Hardware wallet (a small device, e.g. Ledger, Trezor)
Get the wallet from the official website (type the address yourself or use the link from…

scenes.vo: Two kinds of wallet: Safe install: Prove the backup works (do this now, with nothing in the wallet): remove the wallet (or use a second device), choose "restore/import", enter your written seed phrase, and check the same address appears. First, Software wallet (browser extension or phone app, for example MetaMask, Rabby): free, convenient; keys live on your computer/phone. Next, Hardware wallet (a small device, for example Ledger, Trezor): keys stay on the device; every transaction must be approved on its screen. Recommended once you hold more than you'd be upset to lose. Buy only from the manufacturer's official website, never second-hand. Then, Get the wallet from the official website (type the address yourself or use the link from the official site). Fake wallet apps and sponsored search ads are a common scam. Also, Create a new wallet. Never use a seed phrase someone else gave you or that came pre-printed in a box. On top of that, Write the seed phrase on paper (or stamp it into metal), in order, spelled exactly.

items: Store it somewhere private and safe from fire and water
Never store it in photos, email, notes apps, cloud drives or password managers.

scenes.q: A wallet box contains a card with 24 words already printed. What do you do?
scenes.a: Don't use it. It's a scam. Genuine devices generate your seed phrase themselves.

scenes.q: Is a cloud-drive photo of your seed phrase a safe backup?
scenes.a: No. Anyone who gets into that account can take everything.
